basic_identification.full_title: Mild Steel Wire Rod for General Engineering Purposes — Specification (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering (approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Wrought Steel Products Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements of hot-rolled mild steel wire rods in coils [1]. Under the second amendment, the scope is restricted strictly to coils [1], removing straightened and cut lengths.
scope.page_number: Page 1 of base standard & Page 1 of Amendment No. 2

revision_history.edition: First Revision (with 15 grades of carbon steels introduced)

amendment_slips.description: Updates chemical limits and referenced testing standards.

Substitutes Clause 1 to restrict the scope strictly to hot-rolled mild steel wire rods in coils [1] and replaces Table 1, Note 4 to permit any other restricted chemistry within specified grades upon mutual agreement between the manufacturer and purchaser [1].

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Serves as the referee analytical testing methodology used to verify specified Carbon, Manganese, Silicon, Sulphur, and Phosphorus limits of the grades.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Metallic materials — Tensile testing — Part 1: Method of test at room temperature
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Used to evaluate physical mechanical properties, such as yield strength and ultimate tensile strength (UTS), if requested by the purchaser.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Metallic materials — Brinell hardness test: Part 1 test method
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Referenced to measure and verify Brinell hardness numbers (HBW) of the hot-rolled wire rod coils.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: General requirements for the supply of metallurgical materials (second revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Establishes baseline commercial trade, supply chain, inspection, and technical delivery conditions for the wire rods.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Random sampling and randomization procedures (first revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Prescribes statistical randomization methods to select unbiased sample coils from manufacturing batches for quality control audits.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Standardises the mathematical rounding of observed or calculated testing values to determine standard limits.

allied_standards.title: Mild steel wire for general engineering purposes — Specification
allied_standards.relevance: The national standard for general engineering wires (e.g. binding wire, mesh, nails), which specifies that the raw input material used should conform to IS 7887.

allied_standards.title: Steels for cold heading/cold extrusion application: Part 1 Wrought carbon and low alloy steels
allied_standards.relevance: Governs carbon and low-alloy steel wire rods optimized for cold-heading processes such as bolts, screws, and fasteners.

allied_standards.title: Carbon steel wire rods — Specification (second revision)
allied_standards.relevance: Specifies high carbon steel wire rods intended for drawing high-strength wires (such as spring wire or wire ropes), as opposed to mild steel.

allied_standards.title: Specification for Mild Steel Wire Rod for the Manufacture of Machine Screws (By Cold Heading)
allied_standards.relevance: Details specialized high-ductility mild steel wire rods manufactured specifically for cold-headed machine screws.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India, all mild steel wire rods used for general engineering purposes in India must conform to IS 7887:1992 and bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, stocking, selling, or importing non-certified wire rods is a legal offence. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to heavy metallurgical products as it is reserved strictly for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.

requirements.detail: Wire rod coils conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) stamped permanently on a secure metal tag attached to each coil.

Ladle analysis must conform to the strict chemical composition thresholds defined in Table 1 for 15 specified grades. Delineated parameters cover Carbon, Manganese, Sulphur, Phosphorus, and Silicon limits. For example, common Grade 2 limits Carbon to 0.08% max, and Manganese to 0.25 - 0.40% with Silicon at 0.15 - 0.35%.

By mutual agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser, any other restricted chemical composition limits within specified grades can be defined to suit downstream drawing or fabrication needs [1].
Hot-rolled wire rods must satisfy strict dimensional limits to prevent drawability failure: nominal size tolerances must be within ±0.40 mm max, and out-of-shape variance must not exceed 0.60 mm max.
The wire rods must be clean, homogeneous, and entirely free from harmful surface defects such as cracks, seams, piping, deep scratches, or severe scale that would compromise cold-drawing performance.
If any sample fails a physical or chemical test, two additional samples must be drawn from the same lot. Both retests must pass for the lot to be accepted; otherwise, it is rejected [2].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 7887 : 1992 is the strict national Indian Standard specification governing hot-rolled mild steel wire rods supplied in coils for general engineering and downstream wire drawing (such as nails, binding wire, and mesh). Under India's national Steel Quality Control Order, all such wire rods must bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). The standard establishes chemical compositions for 15 carbon steel grades, allows customized restricted chemistries on mutual agreement per Amendment No. 2 [1], sets tight dimensional tolerances, and mandates strict surface and testing controls to ensure seamless drawability without mechanical failure.
